assessments.reasoning: LaTeX Project 1.3a original, acquisition 88d1ee2f21bd44659ed6cedbf27d8abf. Connector range [5232,7418), SHA-256 7a178b7879f129bc56646c00592607c55f2bf3798fea3880d6b4b0cc0b6a708f, covers clause 6’s opening qualifications and both 6(d) options. The complete text supplies the definitions and surrounding distribution routes.

challenge.method: Tested mandatory bundling, a Current Maintainer distribution under clause 4, component exemptions, compiled distribution under clause 7, alternative licensing under 10(a) and possible importation of the 1.3c non-replacement passage.
challenge.results: Equivalent access from the same or a similar place satisfies the first option in the designated-place case, even if recipients never copy the original. Sufficient information independently satisfies the second. Clause 7 refers back to clause 6 and 10(a) preserves its conditions regarding the Work. The separately inspected 1.3a text contains no counterpart to 1.3c’s express non-replacement exception.

limitations: Clause 6 applies to a distributor who is not the Current Maintainer. Only the Current Maintainer may add a clear, condition-specific exemption in a component’s copyright notice. The claim covers one condition of distribution.
reasoning: Clause 6(d) requires at least one of two things with the Derived Work where clause 6 applies. The distributor may supply a complete unmodified copy of the Work or information sufficient to obtain that copy.
